text:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — locking down the traffic-lab config for the kernel-selection QoS calibration. Need apples-to-apples across A100/RTX pools.
Kevin Patel: SG. What's the minimal config we need identical (besides weights)?
Zach Gomez: model name, sequence-length distro, seed, kv-warmup policy, batching window, driver CPU affinity, and runtime build hash.
Lisa Huang: Add kernel_policy (AUTO / FORCE-F16 / FORCE-INT8) + CUDA driver + env vars in the repro key.
Maria Chen: Proposed single-file scenario for replay harness:
```
seed: 2024
qps_ramp:
  start: 10
  peak: 200
  ramp_secs: 120
microbursts:
  - t: 45
    multiplier: 5
    width_s: 4
  - t: 160
    multiplier: 4
    width_s: 8
seq_len_dist:
  p50: 64
  p90: 256
  p99: 512
kv_warmup:
  policy: prefix
  duration_s: 60
batching:
  max_latency_ms: 6
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
kernel_policy: AUTO
runtime_hash: r2024d9
```
perf-bot: test queued on traffic-lab-2 for 05:00 UTC :gear: 
Maria Chen: KV note: prefix warmup replays first N tokens to populate KV. Previously reduced p99 by ~25 ms for seq>256.
Kevin Patel: Make sure kernel selector sees identical telemetry inputs. A slight seq-hist drift can flip picks.
Zach Gomez: We should log per-request: kernel_id, batch_size, kv_hit, seq_len, and include that in traces for correlation.
Lisa Huang: Recent batching change (8ms -> 6ms) cut median but p99 worsened at peak. Hypothesis: smaller window -> fewer warm, smaller batches -> kernel warmup miss.
Maria Chen: Instrumented runtime to emit per-token GPU/CPU time, KV hit/miss, selected kernel and batch composition. Regression aligns with increased small-batch fraction during spikes.
Kevin Patel: Plan: controlled matrix toggling only batching.window and kernel_policy. 5 repeats each. Compute mean p50/p95/p99 and run KS test on latency CDFs.
Zach Gomez: I'll add a microburst-only scenario: 90s baseline at 10 QPS then 6 spikes of 8x for 3s each to stress batching & KV.
perf-bot: experiment 3623456789-01 started on traffic-lab-2
Lisa Huang: For analytics, generate CSV with columns: run_id,kernel_policy,batch_window_ms,avg_batch_sz,kv_hit_rate,p50,p95,p99,throughput,seed,repeat. Easier to diff.
Maria Chen: Repro keys: OS kernel, CUDA driver, runtime_hash, relevant envs (LD_PRELOAD, TF/CUDA flags). Small driver diffs change kernel latencies.
Kevin Patel: Should we mask cold-start period (first 30s) for final metrics? Some runs have allocator/JIT noise.
Zach Gomez: Masking OK if applied consistently. I prefer both raw and masked metrics in the artifact.
Lisa Huang: If kernel selection looks suboptimal, next step: force each kernel and compare perf + output parity on the same trace.
Maria Chen: Kicking off matrix: kernel_policy in [AUTO, FORCE-F16, FORCE-INT8] x batch_window in [6,8] ms x 3 repeats. Will upload CSV + per-request traces.
Kevin Patel: Ping me with S3 path for traces; I'll run batch-size vs kernel-id correlation and a small PCA over telemetry.
Maria Chen: TL;DR: strict seed + identical runtime/env + per-request kernel logging + synthetic ramps + microbursts. Goal: remove confounding signals so kernel selection perf comparisons are apples-to-apples.
perf-bot: experiment 3623456789-01 finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-traffic-lab/3623456789/3623456789-01.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
